title: Service-Anchored Onboarding Eval Contract with Regression Contingency
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview
========
This document defines a service-anchored evaluation contract used during model onboarding and promotion for production serving. It couples acceptance criteria (quality, latency, token-cost) with an explicit regression contingency playbook so that any release can be validated and, if necessary, automatically mitigated or rolled back with low human overhead. The goal is to make onboarding decisions auditable, repeatable, and safe across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployment modes.

Why a service-anchored contract?
- Aligns model promotion to concrete product-facing SLOs rather than abstract metric thresholds.
- Ensures cross-functional sign-off (SRE, Product, Applied ML, Platform) with traceable artifacts.
- Ties continuous evals, shadow traffic, and canary sampling to an actionable regression escalation path.

Scope
-----
Applies to:
- New model variants promoted to staging/canary for inference (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Quantized artifacts and hybrid-precision builds.
- Functional changes to prompt templates or response post-processing that affect user-visible outputs.

Exclusions:
- Research-only checkpoints not intended for production.
- Infrastructure-only kernel upgrades that do not change model weights or prompt behavior (see infra change process).

Core concepts and definitions
----------------------------
- Service owner: owner of the product endpoint (e.g., search-relevance, chat-assistant).
- Eval contract: a checklist and thresholds mapping to service SLOs used to accept or reject a promotion.
- Shadow validation: live traffic duplicated to the candidate model with telemetry capture only (no user-facing outputs).
- Regression: any statistically significant negative delta in an agreed-upon slice of metrics that crosses the impact budget.

Eval contract template (summary)
------------------------------
1) Identify service-critical slices (owners):
   - Top-5 tenant workflows by volume (owner: Product).
   - Safety and compliance slices (owner: Security).
   - High-cost long-context queries (owner: Platform).

2) Required telemetry and probes:
   - Probe suite: stable probes + 3 exploratory probes per slice. Maintain probe IDs and provenance.
   - Shadow replay: 24h continuous shadow with sampling rate >= 1% of production requests for high-volume services, >= 5% for intermittent services.
   - Token accounting: per-request token counts and per-route cost estimate.

3) Acceptance thresholds (example mapping):
   - Quality: weighted accuracy/utility delta <= -1.5% relative to baseline across critical slices.
   - Latency: 95th percentile latency increase <= 15% or +150ms (whichever smaller).
   - Cost: per-1k-token cost increase <= 10% unless explicitly approved by Finance.
   - Embedding drift: cosine similarity degradation <= 0.02 relative to baseline for retrieval slices.

4) Quantization and hybrid artifacts:
   - Artifact must pass the per-workload quant-sanity checks (see Quant Sanity Checklist GUID).
   - If quantized, run the quant-fallback sentinel (a 1-hour live replay comparing float vs quant responses for a stratified sample).

5) Rollout policy:
   - Canary: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over a minimum of 48h with stability gates at each step. Gates evaluate contract thresholds and critical alert rates.

Acceptance criteria (detailed)
-----------------------------
- A promotion job must produce an immutable evaluation report (artifact id, commit sha, eval-run id) containing:
  - Probe pass/fail table with confidence intervals.
  - Per-slice delta table for quality, latency, cost, safety checks.
  - Annotated examples for any failing probes or >0.5% quality regressions.

- Admission rule: all critical slices must be green OR have an approved exception with documented compensating controls (e.g., fallback model pinned, additional caching).

Regression contingency playbook (operational)
-------------------------------------------
This playbook defines automated and human-in-the-loop steps when a promotion or canary triggers a regression.

Severity classification: 
- Sev-1 (production impact): user-visible correctness failures affecting >0.5% of requests or a spike in error rate causing >0.5% request failures.
- Sev-2 (degradation): quality delta between 0.2%–0.5% on critical slices or latency increases approaching thresholds.
- Sev-3 (observability/noise): alerts with low user impact, requires investigation.

Immediate automated responses (system):
1) Canary abort: if any Sev-1 condition observed during canary window, abort rollout and trigger rollback to previous stable variant.
2) Auto-fallback: route traffic away from candidate to fallback model variant if configured (per-route fallback priority).
3) Telemetry snapshot: capture full request/response KV cache context, token accounting, model logits, and probe ids for 2x the default retention window for the affected slices.

Human triage flow (steps):
1) Pager notification to the oncall evaluation engineer + service owner. Include eval-run id and link to artifact and example failures.
2) Quick triage (15 minutes): run targeted regression bisect (e.g., split by prompt family, device, tenant) using the bisect harness.
3) Decide: rollback, apply runtime mitigation (e.g., revert prompt change, reduce temperature, enforce prefix-caching), or accept with exception. Document decision & mitigation in the eval artifact.
4) Postmortem: for Sev-1 events, publish a short 72-hour incident and a retro within 7 days with root cause and regression fix plan.

Investigation checklist (for triage)
-----------------------------------
- Confirm reproducibility with: shadow-replay --seed <eval-run-id> --slice <slice-id> --compare baseline,candidate
- Check KV cache divergence and cold-start ratios.
- For quantized artifacts, run float-vs-quant diff for annotated failing examples.
- Check prompt pipeline changes and templating fallbacks.
- Inspect recent infra rollouts or kernel updates (cross-reference infra release id).

YAML: minimal eval-run job example
--------------------------------
```yaml
job: promoted-eval-run
service: chat-assistant
baseline_model: rdx-chat-v2.1
candidate_model: rdx-chat-v2.2-qat
probes: [critical-slice-suite, safety-suite]
shadow_sampling: 0.02
metrics: [accuracy_delta, p95_latency_delta, token_cost_delta]
artifact_output: gs://redwood-evals/promotions/2026/rdx-chat-v2.2-qat/report.json
```

Monitoring, alerts and dashboards
--------------------------------
- Dashboards: per-service promotion dashboard with live delta gauges for the contract metrics and a probe failure timeline.
- Alerts (examples):
  - PROMO:sev1_quality_regression -> trigger canary_abort and page evaluation-oncall.
  - PROMO:latency_p95_jump -> page platform-oncall if > 2x baseline for 30 minutes.
  - PROMO:token_cost_excess -> inform finance and owner if > 15% increase sustained for 2 hours.

Reference SLO mapping table (text depiction)
-------------------------------------------
| Service SLO            | Eval Contract Metric           | Threshold/Action | Owner |
|------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------|-------|
| Chat assistant latency | p95 latency delta             | <= +150ms        | SRE   |
| Retrieval recall       | embedding similarity degradation| <= 0.02         | ML    |
| Search relevance       | NDCG@10 delta                 | >= -1.5%         | Product|

Governance and approvals
------------------------
- Promotion requires signoff from: Service owner (acceptance), Applied ML owner (model cert), SRE (capacity/latency acceptance), Security (safety checks) — recorded via the promotion ticket with artifact links.
- Exceptions: any accepted exception must include a compensating control, a sunset date, and a rollback trigger.

Data provenance and auditability
--------------------------------
- Every promotion must include immutable artifacts: model checksum, quantization recipe id, eval-run id, probe-suite version, and the promotion ticket id.
- Audit records are stored in the Promotions Ledger with retention policy 2 years for exec review.

Operational notes and tips
-------------------------
- Prefer shadow validation with real KV context for cache-sensitive services — synthetic probes miss cache-interaction regressions.
- When evaluating quantized builds, prioritize worst-case examples (long context, multi-turn state) in the probe set; these often surface sequence-dependent degradation.
- Use prioritization scores for probe sampling to keep cost bounded: critical slices keep 100% of probe runs, exploratory probes are budgeted at 10% of runs.

Appendix A: Quick rollback commands
----------------------------------
- Abort canary and pin previous variant (CLI):
  redwood promote abort --service chat-assistant --promote-id <promote-id>
  redwood route pin --service chat-assistant --variant rdx-chat-v2.1

- Trigger immediate auto-fallback to float variant for quantized builds (if configured):
  redwood fallback enable --service chat-assistant --from-variant rdx-chat-v2.2-qat --to-variant rdx-chat-v2.2-float --duration 30m

Appendix B: Example post-promotion record (JSON snippet)
------------------------------------------------------
```json
{
  "eval_run_id": "eval-2026-01-27-09-13",
  "baseline": "rdx-chat-v2.1",
  "candidate": "rdx-chat-v2.2-qat",
  "outcome": "aborted",
  "reason": "sev1 quality regression on payment_flow slice",
  "artifact_link": "gs://redwood-evals/promotions/2026/rdx-chat-v2.2-qat/report.json"
}
```
